tasks.gr12-end-of-cold-war-t3: Topic: The end of the Cold War and the events of 1989 for Grade 12 History (CAPS Topic 6). Cover Gorbachev's reforms (glasnost and perestroika, from March 1985), the end of the war in Afghanistan (15 February 1989), Solidarity and the Polish elections of 4 June 1989, the opening of the Berlin Wall (9 November 1989) and German reunification (3 October 1990), the failed coup of August 1991 and the end of the Soviet Union (Gorbachev resigned on 25 December 1991), and the turning point for South Africa (the New York Accords of 22 December 1988, Namibian independence on 21 March 1990, De Klerk's speech of 2 February 1990, Mandela's release on 11 February 1990). Present the reasons for the end of the USSR and for change in South Africa as debated, with several causes weighed; do not name a single cause. Ask factual, cause and source-skills questions.
tasks.gr12-new-world-order-t3: Topic: A new world order for Grade 12 History (CAPS Topic 6). Cover globalisation, the IMF and World Bank (Bretton Woods, 1944), the WTO (1 January 1995), the IT revolution, the balance of power and Africa (North-South and South-South relations), BRICS (first summit 2009, South Africa joined 2010), reactions to globalisation (civil-society resistance such as the Seattle protests of 30 November 1999, environmental groups and the Rio Earth Summit of 1992, nationalism, extremism and the attacks of 11 September 2001), and South Africa's reconciliation (the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, 1995) and unfinished liberation. Present supporters' and critics' views of globalisation fairly. Ask factual, cause and source-skills questions.
